> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3175b3b0a05abdda6131ab85e61be9918cfaf951` — the merge of head `edf7ad87787b2a7f92c6e46e6c27bc2b9bed085c` into base `53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3175b3b0a05abdda6131ab85e61be9918cfaf951 && git checkout 3175b3b0a05abdda6131ab85e61be9918cfaf951
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 edf7ad87787b2a7f92c6e46e6c27bc2b9bed085c && git checkout -B drift-repro 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 && git merge --no-ff edf7ad87787b2a7f92c6e46e6c27bc2b9bed085c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

✅ ACCEPT: PR #23717 at `edf7ad8778` (#23702), round 0. Every check on this head is green or a roster skip. No contract review is owed · 2026-10-15T19:33Z

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU` · holder of claim `6198936128`. Report: the `os-dev-report` `6200357984` on #23702.

**Checklist, read against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report:**
- **PR shape:** draft, base `main`, title `fix(runtime):`, assignee `sunhaolin`. Line 1 is `Fixes #23702`, the body's only closing keyword. Line 2 is `Clause-②: no`.
- **Scope:** 4 files, +579 / −4, inside the claim's surface:
  - the ONE upstream change, in `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts`;
  - two new pin files;
  - one changeset.
  - The shared key `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope` is NOT changed, so seat 1's #23701 is unaffected. `packages/mcp`, `errorFromThrown` and `metadata-protocol` are untouched.
  - `check-governed-merges --pr 23717`: NOT governed. `git merge-tree` is clean against `origin/main` `4c21e57169`.
- **The fix, read in the diff (the sandbox boundary, read with care):**
  - **Holding:** `hostErrorToVm` holds a dup of the VM handle an engine refusal becomes. It holds only for the class the doors key on, asked through the same shared predicate on the HOST-side error, plus a snapshot of everything that crosses back out (`name`, `message` and the `SANDBOX_ERROR_PASSTHROUGH` fields).
  - **The wrapper:** its completion value is now the body's own promise (`SETTLE`, the same two handlers; the body source stays on line 2, so line numbers hold).
  - **Matching:** when `__error` is set, the pump loop reads THAT promise's rejection reason (`getPromiseState`). It throws the host's own `DuplicateRecordError` only on `vm.eq` identity with a held refusal AND an unchanged snapshot.
  - **Why a body cannot forge it:** the line is drawn on the object a host call handed in, never on text or a body-writable global.
    - A forged `name`, a copied field, a rewritten engine error, or a body writing `__error` while its promise fulfils all keep today's `SandboxError` relay.
    - A getter that throws or loops fails the snapshot read, and the relay falls back to the old path.
    - Even a forged match can only report the engine's own refusal: nothing is widened.
  - **Handles:** the body promise and every held dup are released in the `finally` before `vm.dispose()`. The fulfilled-non-promise case does not double-dispose.
  - Every other host error crosses exactly as before.
- **Pins and reverse verification:**
  - 11 unit pins (identity `toBe` for uncaught, re-thrown and held-then-thrown, the hook origin, six speaker controls, and an unrelated `404` that stays a `SandboxError`).
  - 6 door rows on `POST /api/v1/actions/udoc/:action` over a real engine and runner: uncaught, re-thrown, held, a hook body, two VM hops, and the speaker controls.
  - Ablation 1 (the identity relay no-oped) turned exactly the 8 positive rows red, with every control green. Ablation 2 (the snapshot half removed) turned exactly the two rewritten-error controls red. Both restores were proven against HEAD.
- **Changeset prose, sentence by sentence:** `@objectstack/runtime` `patch`, `fix(runtime):`, `Clause-②: no`, the same level and grade as its siblings `23686-dispatcher-unique-violation.md` and `23587-hono-unique-violation.md`.
  - The TO's `details` (`developerMessage`, `object`, with no `field`) is what the dispatcher answers for a host-code handler's write on the same object. Its pin `dispatcher-unique-violation-wire-code.test.ts` adds `field` only when the engine's error states a column.
  - The in-process note (callers now catch the engine's `DuplicateRecordError`, with no `innerMessage` and no wrapper) matches the diff.
- **Gates:**
  - **Local, at `edf7ad8778`:** 61 derived, 61 run, 0 unmeasured, all exit 0. The runtime suite: 392 files, 5895 passed. `test:repo`: 808 passed. The typecheck exits 0.
  - **Gate evidence: the check-runs pinned to `edf7ad8778`, read at this stamp.** 40 distinct checks: 34 `success`, including Lint · ESLint, the Type Check family, all six Test Core shards, Build Core, Check Changeset and Governed Surface Queue Guard, and 6 skipped. All 6 skips are roster names: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. Nothing is running and nothing failed.
- **Contract review:** none owed. `Clause-②: no`, and `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` derives `TIER_DEFAULT` with no schema or governed face. The ruled spelling already governs every route; this restores it at the sandbox relay.

**Hypotheses:**
- **(a) holds:** the engine raises the error host-side, so identity is honest. The fork did not arise.
- **(b) holds:** the `DuplicateRecordError: ` prefix is gone from the client sentence.
- **(c):** hooks cross and are pinned. Flow script nodes do not run the sandbox, by reading. `/data` (`mapDataError`, at function level) now names the object the engine refused.

**Accepted deviations:**
- lint narrowed, with its three pieces of evidence;
- scratch rigs deleted before the gates, never pushed;
- a second ablation leg beyond the order;
- `origin/main` merged once before the PR, with no overlap since.

**Out of scope, filed:** **#23718**. A body that throws a plain object is answered `undefined: <message>` or `[object Object]`, because the reject handler flattens a value with no `name`. It is pre-existing and measured at the action door.

**Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay, in this act. If #23685's driver-memory timeout ejects it, it is not re-queued blind.
